newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close sharply up.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed sharply up on Monday amid dwindling supplies from farms and ginneries at the fag-end of the 1996/97 (July-June) crop year and higher sales tax, dealers said.
The rates rose owing to low supplies and the raise in the sales tax to 12.5 percent from 10 percent from June 13 when the government announced budget for fiscal 1997/98, dealer Nasim Usman said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted for 2,275/2,300 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the K-68 for 2,485/2,500 and the MNH-93 for 2,500/2,510.

The Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said exporters had shipped 102,068 bales (375 lbs each) of cotton by June 14 compared to 1.82 million bales in the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 121,274 bales by June 16 compared to 2.32 million bales in the same time a year ago.
